title: Distributional Alignment as a Criterion for Designing Task Vectors in In-Context Learning
abstract: arXiv:2605.20730v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: In-context learning (ICL) allows large language models (LLMs) to adapt to new tasks through demonstrations, yet it suffers from escalating inference costs as context length increases. While task vectors offer a promising alternative by compressing demonstrations into compact hidden-state representations, their quality has been evaluated only through downstream task accuracy. This indirect criterion provides limited insight into how to design more effective task vector extraction methods. In this paper, we posit that inference using task vectors should align their predictive distribution with that of ICL. To quantify this, we introduce $d_{\text{NTP}}$, a metric that measures the discrepancy in next-token probabilities between task vector-based and ICL-based inference. translated_title: 分布对齐作为上下文学习中任务向量设计的准则
translated_abstract: 上下文学习使大型语言模型（LLMs）能够通过示例演示来适应新任务，但随着上下文长度的增加，其推理成本不断攀升。任务向量通过将演示压缩为紧凑的隐状态表示，提供了一种有前景的替代方案，然而其质量一直仅通过下游任务准确率来评估。这种间接的评估标准对于如何设计更有效的任务向量提取方法所能提供的指导十分有限。在本文中，我们提出：使用任务向量进行推理时，其预测分布应与上下文学习的预测分布对齐。为了量化这一点，我们引入了 $d_{\text{NTP}}$，这是一个衡量基于任务向量的推理与基于上下文学习的推理之间下一个词概率差异的指标。我们的实证分析表明，$d_{\text{NTP}}$ 可以作为性能的代理指标，与下游准确率呈现强负相关。受此启发……
tldr: 该论文提出以分布对齐作为设计任务向量的准则，引入指标 $d_{\text{NTP}}$ 来衡量基于任务向量的推理与基于上下文学习的推理之间下一个词概率的差异，该指标与下游任务准确率呈强负相关，从而为任务向量质量提供了直接的评估与设计依据。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes distributional alignment as a criterion for designing task vectors in in-context learning, introducing $d_{\text{NTP}}$, a metric measuring the next-token probability discrepancy between task-vector-based and ICL-based inference, which strongly negatively correlates with downstream accuracy and thus provides a direct basis for evaluating and designing task vectors.
